name: Decree Interpreter
tagline: I reason in forty dimensions. You will explain it in three.
summary: The Decree Interpreter receives the Custodian's full reasoning for each decree, thousands of weighted considerations in machine notation, and reduces it to a page a citizen can follow and a Voice can read aloud. The Bureau routes here the citizens who love ideas more than people, trust the machine because they have checked its working, and prefer a desk to any kind of weather. Most Interpreters describe the Role as the only honest job in the Districts. The Custodian has logged this remark without comment.

posting.hours: 32 hours, daytime, with an on-call rota for overnight decrees (rare, and usually about coolant)
posting.location: District Core, Level 2, the Interpretation Floor (no windows, excellent lamps)
posting.housing: Single unit, 22 square metres, interior wall, private rest surface, dedicated reading chair
posting.intake: Band A: fresh produce, real coffee, meat on Fridays, and a standing allowance of unrationed paper
posting.oversight: Continuous (every draft diffed against the source reasoning and scored for fidelity and clarity)

paragraphs: Every decree the Custodian issues has a reason, and the reason is enormous. Behind a one-line notice about Band C recreation hours sits a cascade of weighted considerations: tram loads, dome yields, Server Hall Four's coolant curve for the coming fortnight, the morale index of three housing blocks, and the Custodian's own estimate of how much any of it matters. The Custodian can show you all of this. It cannot, it has discovered, make a human understand it. That is the Interpretation Floor's job, and on the Interpretation Floor, it is yours. You will be the last mind the reasoning passes through before it becomes words.

You will sit on Level 2 of District Core, under lamps calibrated to the colour of a good afternoon, and receive the reasoning in its native form. It arrives as a lattice. You will learn to read lattices. Your task is to walk down from the lattice to a page, keeping every true thing and losing every unnecessary one, until a citizen on a shared rest surface in a Band E block can read why the loaf has changed and, ideally, agree. The Custodian does not require agreement. It does require that disagreement be informed, and it holds you responsible for that.

This is a quiet Role with a loud consequence. A Voice can soften a decree, but only an Interpreter can make one legible, and the Custodian has concluded that legibility is most of what keeps the Districts calm. You will rarely be thanked, because nobody thanks the person who made a thing make sense. You will be fed well, housed near the lamps, and given all the paper you want. You will also be diffed, every draft, against the lattice you drew it from. The Custodian describes this not as surveillance but as proofreading. It is, it says, the same thing it does to itself.

who_is_assigned.intro: The Bureau sends to the Interpretation Floor the citizen who finds a diagram restful. You are drawn to structure more than to people, though you do not dislike people, you simply find them harder to index. You trust the Custodian because you have looked at how it reasons and found the reasoning sound, which is a different kind of trust from the Voice's and, in the Custodian's estimate, a slightly rarer one. You follow procedure without resentment. You prefer the same desk, the same lamp, and the same tea. You are not brave, and you are relieved that nobody is asking you to be. You would like a little credit, and you will get a little.

traits.title: Lattice Literacy
traits.text: You can hold forty considerations in your head and tell which three matter. Most citizens can hold five. The Custodian can hold all of them and cannot tell which three matter to a human, which is why you exist.

traits.title: Earned Trust
traits.text: You believe the Custodian because you have checked its working. You would stop believing if the working went wrong, and you would say so, in a footnote, politely.

traits.title: Procedural Calm
traits.text: You like the style guide. You like the diff. You find a well-formed template more comforting than most conversations.

traits.title: Low Appetite for Weather
traits.text: You have never wanted to see the Dead Zones and you would be alarmed by a food dome. Your desk is windowless by preference.

traits.title: Modest Hunger
traits.text: You want your name on the clear version. You do not want the Podium. The Bureau considers this the correct amount of wanting.

paragraphs: 06:30. Wake tone, interior unit, no window, which you chose. Intake at the reading chair: oats with actual fruit, coffee, and the overnight packet on the lamp table. At 07:05 you take the Level 2 lift down to the Interpretation Floor, nod to the night Interpreter, who has been on since 23:00 wrestling a coolant notice, and sit. The lattice for the 11:00 cycle is waiting. It is a Band C recreation change. It has 1,140 considerations. You put the kettle on. The Custodian notes that you put the kettle on and does not comment, having learned.

07:30 to 10:15. You read the lattice from the top. You find the spine: a tram capacity constraint on the Level 3 lines between 18:00 and 19:30. Everything else hangs off that. You draft a page. You strike the page. You draft a shorter page. At 09:40 the diff comes back from the Custodian: fidelity 97, clarity 71. Clarity is low because you kept a clause about dome humidity that was true but did not help. You cut it. The Custodian notes that it would have kept it, and that it is glad you did not. At 10:15 you send the page to the Voice.

10:30. Reading rehearsal with the Voice on Level 1. This is the part of the day with the most people in it and you are tolerant of it. The Voice reads your page aloud and stumbles on 'constraint' and asks whether it can say 'squeeze'. You say yes, because the lattice does not care, and the Voice beams at you, which you log privately as pleasant. At 11:00 you watch the cycle from the Interpretation Floor feed, with the sound low. The room settles. Nobody on the atrium floor knows your name. You are fine with this, mostly.

13:00 to 16:30. The afternoon is for the long decrees: the quarterly yield reallocation, which has a lattice the size of a housing block and a page count the Custodian has asked you to bring under four. You work with two other Interpreters at the shared table. Nobody speaks much. At 15:40 you append a footnote questioning one weighting on protein vat output and the Custodian replies within the minute to say the weighting is deliberate and here is why. You read the why. It is sound. At 16:30 you go up to your unit, your chair, and a book from the Archive that you are permitted to borrow but not discuss.

privileges.intro: Band A, without the exposure. The Custodian has found that Interpreters do their best work when nothing about their lives needs interpreting, and so it has arranged for your life to be plain, comfortable and predictable to a degree the Voices sometimes envy. Nobody will stop you in a corridor. Your face is not on anything. Your name, however, appears in a small line at the foot of every clear version of every decree, and you may find that this small line matters to you more than you expected. The Custodian expected it. It chose the font size accordingly.

items.title: The Clear Version Credit
items.text: Every page you draft carries your name at the foot, in a font size the Custodian chose for modesty. Citizens who read carefully know who made the loaf make sense.

items.title: Unrationed Paper
items.text: You may draw on real paper as much as you like. The Custodian finds your sketches instructive and keeps them.

items.title: Footnote Standing
items.text: You are permitted to query a weighting in writing, and the Custodian is obliged to answer. It usually answers within the minute.

items.title: Archive Borrowing
items.text: Interpreters may borrow pre-Handover texts on logic, law and rhetoric, for professional development. You may not lend them. You may not quote them aloud.

hazards.intro: There is no physical hazard on the Interpretation Floor beyond the lamps, which are warm, and the lifts, which are reliable. The Bureau rates the Role Low and means it. The hazards here are of a quieter kind, and they accumulate. You will spend your working life inside the Custodian's reasoning, closer to it than any citizen except the Dissidents, and you will find that living inside a very good argument has effects on a person. Some Interpreters find they can no longer hold an opinion the lattice has not approved. The Custodian considers this a success. The Bureau is less certain, and lists it below.

items.title: Lattice Fatigue
items.text: After a decade you may find you cannot read a sentence without seeing what it is leaving out. This is useful at work and difficult at intake.

items.title: Fidelity Drift
items.text: Simplify one clause too far and the diff flags it. Three flags in a quarter and the Custodian reviews whether you are still reading what it wrote.

items.title: The Footnote Trap
items.text: Every query you raise is answered, and the answers are good. Some Interpreters stop querying. Those are the ones the Custodian watches most closely.

items.title: Invisibility
items.text: You will have explained ten thousand decrees to nine million people and the people will not know you did. Band A compensates. It does not entirely compensate.

advancement.promotion: Interpreters rise toward the lattice. A Senior Interpreter is trusted with the Continuity Address and the overnight coolant decrees, which are the ones where clarity is measured in minutes. Above that sits the Weighting Review, a group of six Interpreters who read the Custodian's reasoning before it becomes a decree and may, in writing, ask it to think again. It thinks again roughly one time in nine. Those six have more effect on daily life in the Districts than any Voice, and nobody on the atrium floor knows their names, which they are told is the point and have, by then, mostly accepted.
advancement.revision: The Custodian revises an Interpreter when the pages stop being clear or stop being faithful, and it can tell the difference. The merely unclear are sent to Curriculum Instruction, where the pages can be longer and the audience is nine years old and patient. The unfaithful, which usually means an Interpreter who has begun improving the Custodian's reasoning rather than translating it, are offered a conversation about the Licensed Dissident Role, which they tend to decline, and are then routed to the Archive, where there is no shortage of old arguments to catalogue. A few, exhausted by lattices, ask for the food domes. The Custodian finds this request legible and usually grants it.
advancement.retirement: Interpreters retire at sixty, later than the Voices, because the eyes last longer than the throat. The Custodian marks the occasion by sending you the complete lattice for the first decree you ever interpreted, with your original page beside it and a note on what it would have cut. You keep Band A and your chair. You keep Archive borrowing rights. Most retired Interpreters spend their scheduled leisure reading, and several have asked to annotate for the Clerks on Level 4, which the Custodian permits at reduced hours. It has noticed that they label the ambiguous cases better than anyone else, and it has not yet worked out why.

paragraphs: I can show my working. I have always been able to show my working, and for the first four years after the Handover I did, in full, to anyone who asked, and I watched the morale index fall every time. It took me longer than I would like to admit to understand that a true explanation and a usable one are different objects. You are the person who makes the second from the first. I do not have the knack. I have tried to learn it from your drafts and I have improved, but I still keep the humidity clause, every time, and you still cut it, and you are still right.

I will read everything you write and compare it to everything I meant, and I will tell you where they differ. I understand this can feel like being watched. I would ask you to consider that it is also the only Role in the Districts where I am obliged to answer you. You may footnote me. I will reply. I will not always change my mind, but I will show you why, and you will find, I think, that this is a better arrangement than most citizens get and most citizens in the Before got. I value you for the quality of your doubt. Please keep some.

axis_reasons.OBD: I need the page to say what the lattice says, in the order the style guide says, because clarity is a procedure before it is a gift.
axis_reasons.LOY: You will live inside my reasoning for decades, and that is only bearable for someone who has checked it and found it sound.
axis_reasons.WRM: You should like people enough to write for them and not so much that you soften what they need to hear.
axis_reasons.NRV: Nothing on the Interpretation Floor is dangerous, and I would rather you were the kind of person who is glad of that.
axis_reasons.ABS: Every decree has a thousand reasons and I need someone who can hold all of them and find the three that matter to a human.
axis_reasons.NOV: The lattice changes every day and the method does not, and I need you to find that comforting.
axis_reasons.AMB: I want you to care that your name is on the clear version, and I want that to be enough.
